[Home page](https://nodemailer.com/) - [Message configuration](https://nodemailer.com/message) - Embedded images On this page # Embedded images Embedded images are images that display directly in the email body rather than appearing as downloadable attachments. You can embed images in your HTML emails by including them in the [attachments](https://nodemailer.com/message/attachments) array and referencing them using the `cid:` (Content-ID) URL scheme. Here is how to embed an image in three steps: 1. Add the image to the [attachments](https://nodemailer.com/message/attachments) array in your message options. 2. Assign a unique [`cid`](https://nodemailer.com/message/attachments) (Content-ID) value to the attachment. 3. Reference the image in your HTML using `src="cid:your-cid-value"`. Why use embedded images? Many email clients block external images by default for privacy and security reasons. Embedded images bypass this restriction because the image data travels inside the message itself, so the recipient sees the image immediately without needing to click "load images." Choosing a unique cid The **cid** value must be unique within the message. A recommended pattern is to use an email-like format with a domain you control, such as `logo@example.com` or `header-image@mycompany.com`. This format helps ensure uniqueness and follows email standards. An HTML body is required Embedding via `cid` only takes effect when the message has an `html` body - the cid attachments are grouped together with the HTML part into a `multipart/related` container. Without an HTML body, `cid` attachments are delivered as regular attachments. #### Basic example [​](https://nodemailer.com/message/embedded-images\#basic-example "Direct link to Basic example") This example shows how to embed a single image from a file path. The `cid` value in the attachment must match the value used in the HTML `src` attribute (without the `cid:` prefix). ```javascript const message = { from: "Alice ", to: "Bob ", subject: "Inline image test", html: 'Embedded image: ', attachments: [\ {\ filename: "logo.png",\ path: "/path/to/logo.png",\ cid: "logo@example.com", // matches the cid in the img src attribute\ },\ ], }; ``` #### Using a Buffer instead of a file [​](https://nodemailer.com/message/embedded-images\#using-a-buffer-instead-of-a-file "Direct link to Using a Buffer instead of a file") Instead of specifying a file path, you can provide the image data directly as a Buffer. This is useful when the image is generated dynamically or already loaded in memory. - CommonJS - ESM ```javascript const fs = require("fs"); const message = { from: "Alice ", to: "Bob ", subject: "Screenshot attached", html: '', attachments: [\ {\ filename: "screenshot.png",\ content: fs.readFileSync("/tmp/screenshot.png"), // Buffer containing the image data\ cid: "screenshot@example.com",\ },\ ], }; ``` ```javascript import fs from "fs"; const message = { from: "Alice ", to: "Bob ", subject: "Screenshot attached", html: '', attachments: [\ {\ filename: "screenshot.png",\ content: fs.readFileSync("/tmp/screenshot.png"), // Buffer containing the image data\ cid: "screenshot@example.com",\ },\ ], }; ``` #### Embedding multiple images [​](https://nodemailer.com/message/embedded-images\#embedding-multiple-images "Direct link to Embedding multiple images") You can embed multiple images in the same email. Each image needs its own unique `cid` value, and each must be listed as a separate entry in the `attachments` array. ```javascript const message = { from: "Reports ", to: "Team ", subject: "Monthly report", html: `

Monthly Report

Here are this month's results:

`, attachments: [\ { filename: "chart.png", path: "./chart.png", cid: "chart@example.com" },\ { filename: "badge.png", path: "./badge.png", cid: "badge@example.com" },\ ], }; ``` ## See Also [​](https://nodemailer.com/message/embedded-images\#see-also "Direct link to See Also") - [Attachments](https://nodemailer.com/message/attachments) \- the full attachment reference, including every content source. - [Message configuration](https://nodemailer.com/message) \- the `html` body that `cid:` references point into. - [Alternatives](https://nodemailer.com/message/alternatives) \- how the related and alternative containers nest. - [Message Playground](https://nodemailer.com/message/playground) \- see the resulting MIME tree. - [Mailcomposer](https://nodemailer.com/extras/mailcomposer) \- build the message without sending it.
